language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hi there, I am Dracco the drummer.
I am glad that you are here at the music center, because I need your help solving some math problems.
This, for example, is what just happened:
Five musical instruments have appeared with numbers written next to them.
Let’s try to figure out the answer to this math problem.
Next to these five instruments you can see the numbers  that are written.
The total sum of these numbers should be 100. Any mathematical operations can be used;
addition, subtraction, division and brackets ().

Could it be
(7+1) x (7+7) = 112
No, that does not even make 100. Let’s think again...
I think I’ve got it! If you combine 1, 7 and 7, it becomes 177.
If you subtract the other two sevens from 177. Like this (177 - 77) makes 100!
Good work, we got this one sorted.
There are more math problems to be solved.
Are you up for that challenge? Let’s give it a go!

exercises.title: Enough concert seats for all fans?

dialog.text: Meet Classical Classics. They will perform 4 times this year and give several concerts each time. Can you help me find out how many seats we will need for all their fans?

helperSimple.text: Calculate how many seats we need per concert. You will find fractions in your answers. To determine how many seats are needed for each concert, round off the numbers.
